To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) spatial maps are important for understanding ecological processes; (b) the importance of space is often played out at the local-scale, not the broad-scale; and (c) analytical approximations may help identify situations in which the local-scale spatial processes alone are sufficient to understand the broad-scale spatial patterns.

(1) local-scale spatial processes can be important in determining broad-scale patterns and (2) analytical approximations to spatial processes may be able to identify when local-scale processes are sufficient to understand the broad-scale consequences of space.

(a) spatial maps are not necessary to understand spatial processes; (b) local-scale spatial characteristics can be used to approximate the effects of broad-scale spatial maps; and (c) the spatial characteristics that are important to approximate broad-scale spatial maps may be estimated from nature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the spatial patterns of ecological processes.
understanding the importance of local-scale spatial processes in determining the spatial pattern of a population.
the question of whether it is possible to study broad-scale ecological processes using local-scale information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the analytical approximations are only useful when the landscape is not very complex, when there is not too much spatial heterogeneity, and when the spatial pattern of suitable sites does not change over time.
analytical approximations are useful tools for understanding ecological processes, but they should be used with care and with an awareness of their limitations.
the analytical approximation provides a good description of the simulated landscape patterns when the spatial environment is not too complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial map is important, but sometimes we may be able to understand the consequences of space using a summary of the map.
it is possible to study the spatial aspects of ecological processes using coarse spatial information.
it is sometimes possible to understand the ecological implications of broad-scale spatial patterns without having to explicitly map them.
The main takeaway from our work is that
analytical approximations to spatial processes can be used to study ecological patterns when the spatial information needed to simulate the process is unavailable.
it may be possible for analytical approaches to provide useful information about the ecological consequences of spatial patterns.
the spatial environment can play an important role at the local scale in ecological processes.
